stall_speeds_provenance.title: Figure 5.3: Stall Speeds
stall_speeds_provenance.section: Chapter 9 Supplement 4 (gross weight increase from 750 kg to 800 kg; Sensenich propeller; aircraft registered in the USA or Canada), printed page S4-6
stall_speeds_provenance.conditions: Idle, most forward center of gravity, max. weight of 800 kg (1764 lb) - the handbook calls this the most adverse configuration. Speeds in knots; the flap settings are the DA 20-C1's three flap-selector positions, printed on this sheet as Cruise / Take-off / Landing and elsewhere in the manual as CRUISE / T/O / LDG.
stall_speeds_provenance.note: Base Chapter 5 Figure 5.3 (page 5-6) publishes the same table at the 750 kg / 1653 lb gross weight. This module's max gross weight is 1764 lb, so the 800 kg supplement is the governing sheet; the lighter table's speeds are lower and would be optimistic at max gross.

source.doc: Flight Manual, Diamond DA 20-C1, Document No. DA202-C1, Date of Issue 19 December 1997, Revision 20 (August 18, 2005)
source.note: Clean PDF text layer, so no OCR. Chapter 5 PERFORMANCE of this handbook is almost entirely DIAGRAMS: take-off distance, climb performance (cruise / take-off / balked landing), cruising speed and cruising performance are all nomogram carpets of curves, printed once per propeller (Hoffmann HO-14HM-175-157 and Sensenich W69EK7-63 family). Only three ruled grids of printed numbers exist in the whole chapter - airspeed calibration, stall speeds, and the landing/rolling distance table - and of those only stall speeds fits a profile in this pipeline. Performance is carried from Chapter 9 Supplement 4, which raises the gross weight from 750 kg (1653 lb) to 800 kg (1764 lb) and is the governing data for this module: backend/app/data/aircraft_modules/da20.json declares max_gross_weight 1764 and the Sensenich propeller, which are exactly Supplement 4's conditions. Base Chapter 5 publishes the same figures at 1653 lb; using those at a 1764 lb max gross would understate stall speed, the optimistic direction.
